newsitem.title: INDIA: Divestment seen making India firms competitive.
newsitem.headline: Divestment seen making India firms competitive.

text.p: Indian Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Thursday the government's decision to divest some of its stake in profitable state-run firms would help to make them globally competitive.
"The policy and strategy of the United Front government is to support public sector companies with comparative advantage into becoming global giants," Maran told the Indian parliament.
Steps were also being taken to rehabilitate ailing public sector undertakings, Maran said.
He said the government expected to realise 50 billion rupees by divesting such undertakings in the current financial year.

The government recently decided to divest up to 7.5 percent of its holding in India's largest refiner, Indian Oil Corp (IOC), and seven percent in telecommunications monopoly Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL), in two stages.
Officials said these moves followed the government's earlier divestment of 18 percent of its stake in VSNL and eight percent of its holding in IOC.
On Wednesday IOC's board cleared the decks for the government to divest up to 10 percent of its stake in the firm.
Even after the divestment, Maran said, the government would continue to hold a substantial majority in the two firms.
The extent of divestment in the third stage is to be decided by a panel set up in August 1996 to study the cases of 40 public sector undertakings, he added.
